name: eBPF (extended Berkeley Packet Filter)
description: In-kernel virtual machine running verified, JIT-compiled programs at hook points: kprobes, uprobes, tracepoints, perf events, syscall entry/exit, network XDP/tc, cgroup ingress/egress, LSM hooks, sockets. Replaces classic BPF (cBPF) for nearly everything except seccomp filters. The instrumentation primitive behind bpftrace, BCC, Cilium, Falco, Pixie, Hubble. CAP_BPF (5.8+) needed to load programs; CAP_PERFMON for tracing-class.

name: kprobes
description: Dynamic instrumentation that attaches a handler at any kernel instruction address (with a few denylisted instructions). Pre-handler runs before the instruction, post-handler after. Programmable via kernel module, perf-probe(1), or eBPF. The kernel-side hook every dynamic-tracing tool builds on.

name: uprobes
description: Userspace dynamic instrumentation. Attaches at a virtual address inside a binary's text; on hit, kernel notifies the tracer (perf, eBPF). The mechanism behind tracing arbitrary userspace functions without modifying the binary. Used by USDT (User Statically Defined Tracing) probes too.

name: ftrace
description: Built-in kernel function tracer. Plug-in tracers: function (call graph at function entry), function_graph (entry+exit with timing), nop, sched_switch, irqsoff, preemptoff, wakeup. Controlled via /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/ files. trace-cmd(1) is the user-friendly front-end. Used for kernel function-call latency analysis.

name: Tracepoint (static)
description: Compile-time instrumentation point in the kernel — predefined named events (sched_switch, sched_wakeup, irq_handler_entry, syscalls/sys_enter_*, mm/page_alloc, etc.). Stable kernel ABI (unlike kprobes which depend on internal symbols). Subscribed via perf, ftrace, eBPF.

name: perf event counter
description: Hardware (PMU) and software counters tracked per-process or per-CPU. perf_event_open(2) syscall opens an FD; perf(1) wraps. Common: cycles, instructions, cache-references, cache-misses, branch-instructions, branch-misses, page-faults, context-switches, cpu-migrations.

name: Flame graph
description: Brendan Gregg-popularized stack-trace visualization: x-axis = aggregated samples, y-axis = stack depth, width = relative cost. Generated from `perf record -g` → `perf script` → flamegraph.pl. The standard CPU-profile rendering.

name: kdump
description: Kernel-crash dump mechanism. At boot, reserve memory via crashkernel= cmdline; on panic, kexec into a separate 'capture' kernel which writes /proc/vmcore (the panicked kernel's memory) to disk. Typical handler: makedumpfile(8) compresses, then crash(8) analyzes.

name: kexec (fast kernel switch)
description: Switch to a different kernel without firmware reboot. Used by kdump (crashkernel boots the capture kernel via kexec from a panic context) and live kernel updates.

name: Linux audit framework
description: Kernel audit subsystem + auditd userspace daemon. Records syscall / file-watch / privilege events to /var/log/audit/audit.log. Rules via auditctl. Queries via ausearch/aureport. SELinux/AppArmor denials surface here as AVC records.

name: Dynamic debug (dyndbg)
description: Runtime control of pr_debug() statements in kernel. Enable per-file/function/line via /sys/kernel/debug/dynamic_debug/control. Useful for activating verbose driver logging without rebuilding kernel.

name: BPF program types
description: Each program type defines what context (hook) it runs in: BPF_PROG_TYPE_KPROBE, _UPROBE, _TRACEPOINT, _PERF_EVENT, _XDP, _SCHED_CLS (tc), _CGROUP_SOCK, _LSM, _SOCK_FILTER (cBPF). Determines available helpers + verifier rules.

name: BPF maps
description: Key-value stores accessible from BPF programs and userspace. Types: HASH, ARRAY, PERCPU_HASH/ARRAY, LRU_HASH, RINGBUF, PERF_EVENT_ARRAY, STACK_TRACE, CGROUP_ARRAY. The mechanism for BPF programs to keep state and ship results to userspace.

name: BPF verifier
description: Static analyzer the kernel runs on every loaded BPF program. Verifies all branches halt, no out-of-bounds memory access, no unbounded loops, kernel pointer dereferences are safe. Verifier failures are notoriously hard-to-debug ('R1 invalid mem access', 'value pointer arithmetic prohibited').

name: USDT (User Statically Defined Tracing)
description: DTrace-style static probes embedded in user binaries. PostgreSQL, MySQL, OpenJDK, Node, Python, Ruby ship with USDT probes. Hooked via uprobes; bpftrace 'usdt:<binary>:<probe>' syntax.

name: LTTng (Linux Trace Toolkit Next Generation)
description: Production-grade tracer (kernel + userspace). Lower overhead than ftrace under heavy event volume; per-CPU lockless ring buffers. Used in telecom/embedded for always-on production tracing. Out of scope for this leaf (sparse coverage in our corpus).

name: GDB (GNU debugger)
description: Source-level debugger for C/C++/Rust/Go (and many others via runtime support). Breakpoints (`break`), watchpoints (`watch`), single-step, backtrace, register/memory inspection, multi-thread, multi-process, remote-debug via gdbserver, core-dump postmortem. Works with -g compiled binaries.

name: crash (vmcore analyzer)
description: Postmortem kernel debugger. Reads vmcore (kdump output) + System.map + vmlinux. Commands: bt (backtrace), kmem (kernel memory), files, mount, log, irq, runq, rd (read raw memory), sym, dis (disassemble). The standard tool for analyzing kernel panics from production hosts.

name: strace (syscall tracer)
description: Trace syscalls via ptrace(2). Output: syscall name + arg decoding + return value/errno. Powerful for 'why is this program failing': open() returning ENOENT (file missing), connect() returning ECONNREFUSED, etc. -c summarizes; -e to filter; -f to follow forks.

name: ltrace (library call tracer)
description: Like strace but for shared-library function calls. Useful when bug is in libfoo's API rather than the syscall layer. Lower volume than strace usually.

name: lsof (list open files)
description: Lists every open FD in the system: regular files, dirs, sockets, pipes, devices, deleted-but-still-open files. The 'who has /var/log/foo.log open?' tool. -p PID, -c COMMAND, -i :PORT, -u USER.

name: htop (interactive process viewer)
description: Curses-based real-time process monitor. Color-coded CPU/mem bars, tree view, filter (F4), sort (F6), kill (F9), nice/renice. Configurable column set. Replaces top for interactive use.

name: Kernel ring buffer (dmesg)
description: Circular buffer of kernel printk messages — boot logs, OOM killer, segfaults, hardware errors, driver messages. dmesg(1) reads /dev/kmsg. journald also captures and rotates. The first place to look on weird kernel-related symptoms.

name: iostat
description: Per-device disk I/O statistics from /proc/diskstats. Columns: tps (transactions/s), kB_read/s, kB_wrtn/s, %util (saturation). -x adds extended (await, svctm, %iowait). sysstat package; pairs with sar for historical.

name: iotop
description: Per-process I/O usage (like top, but for disk I/O). Reads /proc/<pid>/io. Requires CAP_NET_ADMIN (for taskstats netlink) — typically run as root. Diagnoses 'which process is hammering the disk?'

name: vmstat
description: System-wide virtual memory + processes + IO + CPU stats sampled at interval. Procs (r/b), Memory (swpd/free/buff/cache), Swap (si/so), IO (bi/bo), System (in/cs), CPU (us/sy/id/wa/st). Quick triage tool: high si/so = swapping; high wa = IO bound.

name: pidstat
description: Per-process resource statistics (CPU, memory, IO, context switches, page faults). sysstat package. -d for IO, -r for memory, -w for context switches.

name: blktrace
description: Block-layer I/O tracer. Captures every IO request: queue, merge, getrq, complete, timestamps. Output → blkparse for human-readable, btt for latency analysis. Diagnoses block-layer / IO scheduler / device latency.

name: bpftrace
description: DTrace-inspired high-level eBPF front-end. One-liner syntax: `bpftrace -e 'tracepoint:syscalls:sys_enter_open { printf("%s\n", str(args->filename)); }'`. Compiles to BPF, attaches probes, prints aggregations (count, hist, lhist, stats). Brendan Gregg's go-to.

name: numastat
description: Per-NUMA-node memory statistics. Hits, misses, foreign allocations, local allocations. Diagnoses NUMA-affinity issues on multi-socket boxes.

name: makedumpfile
description: Compresses raw vmcore (kdump output) by stripping zero pages, free pages, cache pages. Reduces 'memory full of zeroes' multi-GB dumps to manageable size. Companion to crash(8).

name: trace-cmd
description: User-friendly ftrace front-end. Commands: record, report, reset, start, stop, extract, list, snapshot. Manages /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/ for you. Output is .dat file (KernelShark can render).

name: Valgrind
description: Userspace memory error and profiling framework. Tools: memcheck (default — leak+invalid-access detection via shadow memory), helgrind/drd (race detection), cachegrind (cache modeling), callgrind (call graph), massif (heap profiling). Slows program 10-50x. Production debugging tool of choice for C/C++ memory bugs.

name: ptrace(2) syscall
description: The kernel mechanism behind strace/gdb/ltrace. Tracer attaches to tracee; on every syscall entry/exit, signal, or memory-modifying event, tracee is suspended and tracer notified. Operations: ATTACH, DETACH, PEEKDATA, POKEDATA, GETREGS, SETREGS, CONT, SYSCALL, SINGLESTEP. Yama LSM restricts who can ptrace whom (kernel.yama.ptrace_scope).

name: bpf(2) syscall
description: Single multiplexed entry point for all BPF operations: PROG_LOAD, MAP_CREATE, MAP_LOOKUP_ELEM, MAP_UPDATE_ELEM, PROG_ATTACH, PROG_DETACH, PROG_TEST_RUN, OBJ_PIN, OBJ_GET, LINK_CREATE. CAP_BPF (5.8+) for most; CAP_PERFMON for tracing-class.

name: perf_event_open(2) syscall
description: Open a counter or event source. Returns FD that can be read for counter values, mmap'd for ring buffer (sample data), or used as target for ioctl (PERF_EVENT_IOC_ENABLE/DISABLE/RESET/REFRESH/SET_FILTER/...). The syscall behind perf(1) and BCC's tracing programs.

name: SIGSEGV (segmentation fault)
description: Signal sent on invalid memory access (null deref, write to read-only, beyond mmap). Default action: dump core + terminate. siginfo.si_addr = faulting address; si_code = SEGV_MAPERR (no mapping)/SEGV_ACCERR (mapping but wrong perms)/SEGV_BNDERR (bound check)/SEGV_PKUERR (pkey).

name: SIGABRT (assertion failure)
description: Self-signal sent by abort(3) or assert(3) failure. Default: core dump + terminate. Indicates a deliberate crash from invariant violation.

name: SIGBUS (bus error)
description: Memory access fault that's not a page fault — usually mmap'd file shrunk under you, or unaligned access on alignment-strict architecture, or NUMA hugepage issues.

name: SIGFPE (arithmetic exception)
description: Despite name, not just floating point — also integer divide by zero, integer overflow (when SIGFPE-on-overflow enabled), invalid float ops. siginfo.si_code distinguishes.

name: Core dump
description: Snapshot of process memory (text, data, stack, heap, all writable mmaps) written to disk on fatal signal. Filename per /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern (or piped to systemd-coredump). RLIMIT_CORE caps size; ulimit -c 0 disables. Use gdb (or crash for kernel) to analyze.

name: perf ring buffer
description: mmap'd memory region holding sample records from perf events. Reader (userspace tool) consumes; producer (kernel) writes. -m/--mmap-pages controls size. Overflow drops samples (visible as PERF_RECORD_LOST).

name: BPF ring buffer (BPF_MAP_TYPE_RINGBUF)
description: 5.8+ replacement for BPF_MAP_TYPE_PERF_EVENT_ARRAY. MPMC ring shared between BPF programs and userspace. Variable-size records, ordering preserved across CPUs. Replaces the per-CPU perf-event array for cleaner aggregation.

name: /proc/<pid>/stack
description: Current kernel-side call stack of the process (if it's in kernel). Useful for diagnosing 'D state' (uninterruptible sleep) — see what kernel function it's stuck in.

name: /proc/<pid>/wchan
description: Symbolic name of kernel function the process is sleeping in. Quick read for D-state diagnosis (e.g. 'nfs_wait_on_request' = stuck waiting for NFS).

name: /proc/<pid>/syscall
description: Currently-executing syscall number + args. Useful for 'what's this hung process doing?' without attaching strace.

name: GDB breakpoint / watchpoint
description: Breakpoint: stop execution at code address. Watchpoint: stop on memory read/write/access. Hardware watchpoints use CPU debug registers (limited count, no perf cost). Software watchpoints single-step (huge perf cost). gdb auto-picks; `set can-use-hw-watchpoints 0` forces SW.

name: GDB backtrace
description: `bt` (or `where`) prints frames from current location up the call stack. Requires DWARF debug info (-g) or at least frame pointers (-fno-omit-frame-pointer). Without either: backtrace lies (misses inlined functions, stops early).

name: GDB threading
description: `info threads` lists all threads of process; `thread N` switches; `thread apply all bt` prints backtrace per thread. Combined with non-stop mode lets you debug one thread while others run.

name: Symbol resolution
description: Mapping address → function/variable name. Symbols come from ELF .symtab (full) or .dynsym (exported only). Stripping (`strip`) removes .symtab. Debug info (DWARF) lives in .debug_* sections — separable into .debuginfo files (GDB auto-loads from /usr/lib/debug/.build-id/).

name: DWARF debug info
description: Standard format for source-level debug info: variables, types, functions, source line numbers, frame info. Requires -g compile flag. Optional split-debug (.debug section in separate file) reduces production binary size.

name: Frame pointer vs DWARF unwinding
description: Two ways to walk the stack: frame pointers (RBP/EBP register chain — small perf cost, no debug info needed) or DWARF .eh_frame info (no perf cost but requires unwinder + complete DWARF). Modern compilers default to no frame pointer for performance; `perf record -g` defaults to DWARF unwinding. -fno-omit-frame-pointer restores reliable backtraces.

name: Sampling vs tracing
description: Sampling: periodically capture state (PC, stack); statistical, low overhead, may miss rare events. perf record (default) is sampling. Tracing: capture every event (every function call, every syscall); complete data, high overhead. ftrace function tracer is tracing. Different problems need different approaches.

name: On-CPU vs Off-CPU profiling
description: On-CPU: where time is spent computing (CPU samples while running). Off-CPU: where time is spent NOT running — blocked on IO, locks, sleep. Brendan Gregg's USE method emphasizes the off-CPU time, which classic profilers (gprof, perf record default) miss entirely.

name: Context switch
description: CPU swap from one task to another. Voluntary: task blocked (waiting). Non-voluntary: preempted (timeslice up or higher-priority woke). High non-voluntary = CPU oversubscription. /proc/<pid>/status voluntary_ctxt_switches + nonvoluntary_ctxt_switches.

name: Process state R (sampling)
description: A sampler that catches a thread in state R is on-CPU. Off-CPU = anything else (S/D/T). The basis of off-CPU flame graphs: subtract on-CPU from wall time.

name: Audit rule (auditctl syntax)
description: `-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S openat -F path=/etc/shadow -k shadow_access` = audit every openat of /etc/shadow with key 'shadow_access'. Rules persist via /etc/audit/rules.d/*.rules (or audit.rules) loaded at boot.

name: Audit record types
description: SYSCALL (system call), AVC (SELinux/AppArmor decision), USER_LOGIN, CRED_ACQ, ANOM_PROMISCUOUS, MAC_POLICY_LOAD, etc. Each event = group of records sharing msg-id. ausearch -m TYPE filters.

name: Kernel panic
description: Unrecoverable kernel state. Kernel printk()s panic message + register dump + stack trace, then halts (or reboots if panic= sysctl set). On modern systems, kdump captures vmcore for analysis.

name: Kernel oops
description: Recoverable kernel error (e.g. NULL deref in module). Kernel logs trace, taints itself, and tries to continue (often the offending task is killed). dmesg shows 'BUG:' or 'Oops:'. Tainted kernel is suspect for further bugs — bug reports require untainted kernels.

name: Process D state (uninterruptible sleep)
description: Cannot be killed (even SIGKILL). Stuck in kernel waiting for IO completion. /proc/<pid>/stack + /proc/<pid>/wchan show what kernel function. NFS hangs, broken disks, kernel bugs land here. Often only resolution: reboot.

name: Process T state (stopped)
description: Suspended via SIGSTOP/SIGTSTP. Resumed by SIGCONT. Sometimes seen because debugger attached (then it's 't' lowercase = traced).

name: Process Z state (zombie)
description: Process exited; awaiting wait() by parent. Holds /proc entry only — no memory, no FDs. Common in containers when pid 1 doesn't reap (the docker init problem).

name: Tracer-attached state
description: When ptrace() attaches, tracee state changes per signals. Visible as 't' (lowercase) in ps. Tracer must explicitly continue (PTRACE_CONT) for tracee to resume.

name: BPF program loaded state
description: BPF program lives in kernel after PROG_LOAD; visible via `bpftool prog show`. Detached but still loaded if no link. Pinned to bpffs to survive program exit.

name: Audit enabled state
description: auditctl -e {0|1|2} sets audit subsystem. 0=off, 1=on, 2=on+locked (cannot disable until reboot — security mode).

name: ftrace active tracer state
description: /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/current_tracer = the active plug-in tracer. Default 'nop' = disabled. Set to 'function' or 'function_graph' to capture.

name: eBPF subsystem
description: Kernel infrastructure: verifier, JIT compiler (per-arch), helper functions, map types, link mechanism, bpffs. Enables sandboxed in-kernel programs invoked at hook points without kernel module loading.

name: perf subsystem
description: perf_event_open(2) + per-CPU ring buffers + kernel/events/ code. Foundation of perf(1), bpf-tracing-class programs, intel-pt traces.

name: ftrace subsystem
description: Kernel code/trace + control files at /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/. Per-CPU ring buffers, dynamic-ftrace patches function entry to call __mcount/__fentry__ hook. Plug-in tracers (function, function_graph, irqsoff, etc.).

name: kprobes subsystem
description: Patches kernel instructions to call handler. Pre/post handlers, register access, kretprobes (return probes). The dynamic-trace primitive ftrace/perf/eBPF build on for non-tracepoint sites.

name: uprobes subsystem
description: Userspace dynamic probes. Trap inserted at virtual address; on hit, kernel notifies tracer. Usable from perf, ftrace, eBPF, USDT-aware tools.

name: audit subsystem
description: kernel/audit*.c. Ring of records sent over NETLINK_AUDIT to auditd. Rules in audit_filter_list. Per-tgid/per-syscall filtering.

name: kdump subsystem
description: crashkernel= boot param + kexec_load(2) + crash code under arch/ for capturing memory state on panic. Capture kernel + initrd typically pre-loaded; on panic, kernel kexec()s to capture kernel which writes vmcore.

name: binutils (objdump, nm, readelf, addr2line, strings, c++filt)
description: GNU binary tools. objdump = disassemble + section headers; nm = list symbols; readelf = ELF structure dump; addr2line = address → file:line; strings = printable strings; c++filt = demangle C++ symbols. Indispensable for binary analysis.

name: strace + ptrace pipeline
description: strace uses ptrace(PTRACE_SYSCALL) to stop tracee at every syscall entry/exit, decode args from registers + memory, print, then resume. -k uses libunwind to capture stack at each syscall.

name: GDB + gdbserver + ptrace + ELF
description: gdb client reads ELF + DWARF for symbol/source info; controls tracee via ptrace (or via gdbserver remote protocol). Multi-process and multi-arch.

name: BCC (BPF Compiler Collection) — methodology cross-ref
description: Cross-reference: covered fully in `methodology` domain. iovisor/bcc — Python+Lua tracing tools (execsnoop, biolatency, opensnoop, etc.) using libbpf to compile/load BPF programs. Higher-level than bpftrace for complex programs.

name: kdump kexec_load implementation
description: Per-arch kexec implementation. x86_64 reserves crashkernel= memory at boot, sets up identity-mapped page tables for the capture kernel, registers panic_notifier to invoke machine_crash_shutdown → machine_kexec.

name: BPF JIT compiler
description: Per-arch JIT (x86, arm64, ppc, mips, riscv) translates BPF bytecode to native machine code. Enabled by net.core.bpf_jit_enable. Hardening: net.core.bpf_jit_harden = constant blinding.

name: perf PMU driver
description: Per-architecture/CPU-model code that programs hardware Performance Monitoring Unit registers. Intel core PMU, AMD core PMU, ARM PMU. Limits the max simultaneous counters per CPU.

name: audit NETLINK_AUDIT driver
description: Bridge between kernel audit subsystem and userspace auditd. Records flow over NETLINK_AUDIT socket; auditd writes them to disk.

name: coredump-handler driver
description: Kernel formats process state into ELF core file, then either writes to fs path (kernel.core_pattern starts with normal char) or pipes to userspace handler (core_pattern starts with `|`). systemd-coredump is the dominant pipe-handler.
